cringe: The pacing feels padded: viewers wait several seconds on a static matchup before anything happens.

would_leave_at: around 3.0 s, when the first screen still has not revealed anything
first_impression: Clean-looking nutrition trivia, but it feels too slow and template-driven for a short-form feed.
problems: The hook is only moderately strong because the first frame is a static infographic with no surprising visual or immediate payoff.
Each round takes too long; the viewer waits 4-5 seconds before seeing the answer.
The same layout repeats three times, making the middle of the video feel predictable.
Some type is very small, especially source text and the per-100g labels.
The final summary slide is useful but visually quiet and may be missed after a long buildup.
No actual food imagery, motion, or human touch makes it feel more like a Canva template than a brand social post.
The caption's RecipeFix CTA reads like an unrelated product ad.
fixes: Reveal each answer faster: show the matchup for 1 second, then animate the winner and numbers immediately.
Cut total length to 10-14 seconds, or make it a carousel where each slide has one clean question and answer.
Make the first frame more provocative, e.g. 'A red pepper beats an orange at vitamin C' or 'Which “healthy” guess is wrong?'
Add real food cutouts or simple ingredient photography to make it feel more tactile and less templated.
Vary the three rounds visually with different winner animations, scale changes, or quick result cards instead of the same split-screen every time.
Increase the size of the key numbers and reduce tiny secondary labels.
Move sources to a readable final slide or caption rather than tiny text on every result card.
Either remove the RecipeFix promo or tie it directly to the post with a softer CTA, e.g. 'Want nutrition notes while adapting recipes? Try RecipeFix.'
